dataset_note: Bite force in newtons (N), one internally consistent set verified page-by-page on 2026-10-31. Mammalian carnivores: theoretical maximum bite force at the canine tips, estimated from skull dimensions (dry-skull method), Wroe, McHenry & Thomason 2005 Proc R Soc B 'Bite club' (PMC1564077, Table 1); these are models, not in-vivo measurements. Giant panda: canine value from Christiansen & Wroe 2007 Ecology as quoted on Wikipedia (the paper itself is paywalled; no open copy found, so polar bear, wolverine, honey badger, walrus and domestic dog could NOT be verified and are omitted). Crocodilians: in-vivo measurements at the posterior (molariform) teeth, Erickson et al. 2012 PLoS ONE (PMC3303775, Table 1) — 'avg' is the taxon-representative value, 'max' is the largest individual. Komodo dragon: in-vivo transducer measurement, D'Amore et al. 2011 PLoS ONE. Great white shark: 3-D computer model, Wroe et al. 2008 J Zool (abstract: 'may exceed c. 1.8 tonnes'; 18,216 N as tabulated on de.wikipedia citing that paper). Orangutan: minimum estimate of maximum bite force from seed-breaking forces (Lucas et al. 1994). Human: in-vivo gnathodynamometer measurements (Helkimo, Carlsson & Helkimo 1977 for incisors+molars; Waltimo & Kononen 1993 for molars in young adults). Hippo: no peer-reviewed figure found; only the TV-derived ~8,100 N circulates, unverified. Note that canine (carnivores) and posterior-tooth (crocodilians, human molars) values are not strictly comparable positions.

lion.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Panthera leo, body mass 294.6 kg, BFQ 112; dry-skull estimate

tiger.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Panthera tigris, 186.9 kg, BFQ 127

jaguar.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Panthera onca, 83.2 kg, BFQ 137

leopard.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Panthera pardus, 43.1 kg, BFQ 94

cheetah.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Acinonyx jubatus, 29.5 kg, BFQ 119

spotted_hyena.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Crocuta crocuta, 69.1 kg, BFQ 117. Popular '9,000 N' figures are not from this source.

gray_wolf.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Canis lupus lupus, 34.7 kg, BFQ 136

brown_bear.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Ursus arctos, 128.8 kg, BFQ 78

domestic_cat.note: Wroe et al. 2005 Table 1, Felis silvestris catus, 2.8 kg, BFQ 58

giant_panda.note: Wikipedia: 'a 117.5 kg giant panda had a bite force of 1298.9 Newton (BFQ 151.4) at canine teeth', ref 40 = Christiansen & Wroe 2007 Ecology 88(2):347-358 (dry-skull estimate). Paper itself not opened (paywalled).

saltwater_crocodile.note: Erickson et al. 2012 Table 1, Crocodylus porosus, n=7, mass 36-531 kg (mean 272), TL 202-459 cm; range 1446-16414 N; 16,414 N = 'highest bite force measured in any animal', size of that individual not stated in text (largest in sample 531 kg / 4.59 m).

nile_crocodile.note: Erickson et al. 2012 Table 1, Crocodylus niloticus, n=2, mass 86-87 kg, TL 240-261 cm (sub-adults); range 2914-3172 N. Adult Nile crocs would be far higher but were not measured.

american_alligator.note: Erickson et al. 2012 Table 1, Alligator mississippiensis, n=15, mass 47-297 kg (mean 142), TL 213-372 cm; range 2442-9452 N.

komodo_dragon.note: D'Amore et al. 2011: 'highest at 148.56 N' from 200 bite peaks, 10 captive animals 25-75 kg; pull force up to 336.5 N. Bite is weak for body size.

great_white_shark.note: Wroe et al. 2008 J Zool abstract: 'bite force in large white sharks may exceed c. 1.8 tonnes' (~17,700 N). 18,216 N (rear teeth; 9,320 N front) tabulated on https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bei%C3%9Fkraft citing Wroe et al. 2008, 3,300 kg shark. Computer model, not measured.

orangutan.note: Lucas, Peters & Arrandale 1994 AJPA: seed-breaking force 'about 2,000 N' for Macadamia, 'a minimum estimate for the maximum bite forces in orang-utans'. Captive animals; not a canine value.

human.note: Incisors: Helkimo, Carlsson & Helkimo 1977 Acta Odontol Scand, 125 Skolt Lapps 15-65 y: men 176 N (molar 382 N), women 108 N (molar 216 N). Molars: Waltimo & Kononen 1993 Scand J Dent Res, healthy young adults: men 847 N, women 597 N. Male values used.

hippo.note: No peer-reviewed newton figure found. Blog post (Simply Ecologist, 2023) states 'up to 1,800 psi (8,100 Newtons)' and that only females have been tested; attribution to Brady Barr / National Geographic was NOT confirmed on any page opened. Treat as unverified.

not_verified_omitted.polar_bear: Not in Wroe 2005 table; Christiansen & Wroe 2007 paywalled (Semantic Scholar: no OA PDF; ResearchGate/Academia 403). A press piece even says polar bear was not in that study.
not_verified_omitted.wolverine: Only a forum transcription (~254 N canine) found; not reliable.
not_verified_omitted.honey_badger: No verifiable N figure on any page opened.
not_verified_omitted.german_shepherd: Domestic dog absent from Wroe 2005 table; no verified N figure.
not_verified_omitted.gorilla: Only a blog-cited '3,420 N' (IFAW) found; no peer-reviewed page opened.
not_verified_omitted.chimpanzee: No newton figure found on an opened page.
not_verified_omitted.other_herbivores_and_small_mammals: red_kangaroo, koala, moose, bison, zebra, camel, pig, cow, mouse, rat, hedgehog, vampire bat, dolphin, orca, sperm whale, rhino, elephant: not present in any opened source.
